title: 'A Little Jealous': Sunil Chhetri on India's Historic Chance to Face Brazil and Uruguay
excerpt: The retired India captain admits he never got an opportunity like this in nearly 20 years with the national team, as India prepare to host five-time world champions Brazil in Kolkata.
body:
• Former India captain Sunil Chhetri says he feels "a little jealous" watching the current squad get to face Brazil and Uruguay, an opportunity he never had in his nearly 20-year international career.
  • India will host five-time World Cup winners Brazil on October 3 and two-time champions Uruguay on October 6 at Kolkata's Salt Lake Stadium.
  • Chhetri, 42, dismissed any prospect of a comeback, joking that he "can barely run properly" after a recent training session.
  • India currently sit 138th in the FIFA rankings, with Chhetri calling for optimism and collective responsibility rather than blame.

A Career Without This Stage

Sunil Chhetri has seen almost everything Indian football has to offer. He scored 94 international goals across nearly two decades, captained the side through its highs and lows, and retired in 2025 as one of the most decorated players in the country's history. But there is one experience he never had — facing a footballing superpower.

"I feel a little jealous as a spectator. In my 24-26 years as a professional and nearly 20 years with the national team, I never got an opportunity like this," Chhetri told the All India Football Federation.

India are scheduled to host Brazil on October 3 and Uruguay three days later at Kolkata's Salt Lake Stadium. The fixtures will give a young Indian squad a rare chance to test itself against two of South America's most storied football nations — Brazil with five World Cup titles and Uruguay with two.

Backing the Next Generation

Chhetri, now 42, urged the current players to stay fit, compete with determination, and seize what he called a once-in-a-generation opportunity. Despite stepping away from the national-team setup, he said he remained confident in the squad's emerging talent.

"This is their time. There are so many talented youngsters in the team. Everyone gets their opportunity; just like I got mine 20 years ago."

— Sunil Chhetri

When asked about selection decisions and the omission of certain players, Chhetri declined to second-guess the coaching staff. "The coach has to answer that. I'm just a fan now, watching like everyone else," he said.

He also shut down any immediate prospect of a comeback with characteristic humor: "I just trained for 20 minutes. I'm around 42 now, I can barely run properly and I'm struggling."

Indian Football at a Crossroads

The Brazil and Uruguay fixtures come at a turbulent time for Indian football. The national team sits 138th in the FIFA rankings, and uncertainty surrounds the domestic calendar. Chhetri acknowledged the struggles but called for patience and shared accountability.

"The Indian football graph, for as many years as I've played, has always been like this. We're probably in a phase where things are not going very well, because of what we've done with the national team, what we've done in the league, etcetera. But we all have to be hopeful," he said at the Football Players' Association of India's Indian Football Awards 2026.

"At the end of the day, it's going to be fine. It takes time. Things might be a little bit kharab (bad), but things are going to be fine."

Chhetri also accepted responsibility for the team's decline in rankings during his tenure. "I was also a part of the national team. And why has the ranking gone down? It's because of the way we have played, the games that we should have won but lost. That is the reason why we are where we are. As players, we take responsibility. I took it when I was there."

What These Matches Mean

For India's football fans, hosting Brazil and Uruguay represents a rare moment of global relevance for a sport that remains overshadowed by cricket in the country. The matches at Salt Lake Stadium — a venue with a capacity of over 85,000 — could draw some of the largest crowds for international football in India's recent history.

Whether the current squad can make the most of the opportunity remains to be seen. But as Chhetri put it, the chance itself is what matters. He never got one like it. This generation does.
